subject: Nanotechnology
title: Spintronics Basics
description: A short lesson to help you apply Spintronics Basics.

hook.text: Electrons carry charge, but they also carry spin — a tiny magnetic property that stores information.

buildup.text: Traditional electronics ignores spin. Spintronics uses it — reading data without moving charge through a wire.

discovery.text: Giant magnetoresistance changes a material's resistance based on spin alignment — earning a Nobel Prize in 2007.

twist.text: Spin signals decay over nanometers in many materials — keeping spin coherent is the central challenge.

climax.text: Every hard drive read head uses GMR — spintronics already stores most of the world's data.

punchline.text: Spin the electron and it becomes a bit — no charge flow needed.

quiz.question: What property of electrons does spintronics exploit?
options: Their mass, which varies with speed
Their intrinsic spin, which acts like a tiny magnet
Their color, which changes with energy
